method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across self-forgetfulness and the care of life, the images of fire, seed and candle, mutual care and concrete offerings, teaching and service, faithfulness through trial, the sacrifice of the Manifestation, Abraham and ransom, persecution and martyrdom, grief and inheritance, personal devotion, poetry and prayer, and the ends of sacrifice in human welfare. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Everything becomes yours by Renunciation of everything.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s saying to Julia Grundy that everything becomes yours by renunciation of everything; a concise paradox at the heart of the subject.

selected.text: What does the ocean care about a dewdrop? Whatever oppression has occurred until now has only watered the Blessed Tree.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks what the ocean cares about a dewdrop and says all oppression has only watered the Blessed Tree; a memorable image of growth through suffering.

selected.text: If thou wilt look with the eye of truth, thou wilt see that all stations and conditions in this fleeting world are places of sacrifice, yet the sacrifices differ - one becomes a sacrifice to disease, another a sacrifice to aversion, another a sacrifice to earthly affairs.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes that all conditions in this world are places of sacrifice, but that people become sacrifices to disease, aversion or earthly affairs; reframes the choice of what one is spent for.

selected.text: This is the hour of self-sacrifice for the good of humanity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declares this the hour of self-sacrifice for the good of humanity; widens the closing horizon.

selected.text: Rather, sacrifice yourselves in His path with joy and free will
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids believers sacrifice themselves in His path with joy and free will; supports the introduction’s question of love and freedom.

selected.text: A believer is sometimes called upon to suffer a living martyrdom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells Julia Grundy that a believer is sometimes called to suffer a living martyrdom; names enduring sacrifice in daily life.

selected.text: Suffer them to become soul-sacrificing in the arena of nearness and union
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that others be made soul-sacrificing in the arena of nearness and union; prayer for others to become a gift.

selected.text: The thing we hold most dear is the thing to give. This is real sacrifice.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that the thing we hold most dear is the thing to give, and that this is real sacrifice; a short, self-standing test of sacrifice.

selected.text: of Oneness that thou mayest in all thine affairs become the embodiment of God’s bountiful favours, mayest with heart and soul expend thyself
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: I am not gathering armies of war, rather I am preparing the field of sacrifice.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declares that he is not gathering armies of war but preparing the field of sacrifice; a memorable contrast with warfare.

selected.text: O my Lord! I desire to lay down my life in Thy path if Thou accept it from me
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer desires to lay down His life in God’s path if He accept it; surrender to the divine will.

selected.text: now that you have sacrificed your beard and its roots in the path of the love of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addresses one who sacrificed his beard and its roots in the path of the love of God; a specific detail of humiliation endured.

selected.text: By God! Through you the tale of sacrifice was renewed, and the Concourse on High lamented
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says that through them the tale of sacrifice was renewed and the Concourse on High lamented; remembrance and lament joined.

selected.text: Whatever befell thee in the path of God hath not been and will never be lost in His sight.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assures one that whatever befell him in the path of God will never be lost in His sight; consolation in trial.

selected.text: This is the fruit of the trees of oneness and the flowers of the rose-garden of uniqueness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls this the fruit of the trees of oneness and the flowers of the rose-garden of uniqueness; closes the linked readings with fruit.

selected.text: in the arena of sacrifice thou wert superior to that legendary champion of the land of Zabul
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells one that in the arena of sacrifice he surpassed the legendary champion of Zabul; a memorable heroic image.

selected.text: l-Adhkar. This purpose is indeed most acceptable. Would that 'Abdu'l-Baha possessed freedom, that he himself might carry the clay and labour in the building of that wall
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wishes he possessed freedom to carry the clay and labour himself on the building of that wall; a concrete example of offering one’s own labour.

selected.text: But the others (the recipients of such love) must also be disinterested and life-sacrificing.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds that the recipients of such love must also be disinterested and life-sacrificing; carries the guide’s question about reciprocal responsibility.

selected.text: Indeed, he sacrificed his soul for Prague and offered his body as an oblation for the friends.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes that he sacrificed his soul and offered his body as an oblation for the friends; pairs a written tribute with the account of fatal nursing.

selected.text: Yet Thou knowest that I have not sought preservation for myself in Thy path, nor rest in Thy love.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer says He has not sought preservation for Himself nor rest in God’s love; the Manifestation’s petition.

selected.text: at every moment he may plunge into the sea of sacrifice, at every hour he may render some service
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that one may plunge every moment into the sea of sacrifice and render some service every hour; opens prayers for others.

selected.text: imprisonment in the path of the Beloved is a palace, and chains and bonds are freedom in both worlds
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says imprisonment in the path of the Beloved is a palace and chains are freedom in both worlds; a memorable paradox from prison.

selected.text: Let each sacrifice himself for the other, that joy may be attained and heavenly delight made manifest
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids each sacrifice himself for the other so that joy and heavenly delight may be made manifest; names joy as the fruit of mutual sacrifice.

selected.text: Would that I had a thousand souls to spend in Thy path, and a thousand lives to sacrifice in Thy love!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer wishes for a thousand souls to spend and a thousand lives to sacrifice in God’s love; memorable devotional longing.

selected.text: I swear by the Resplendent Beauty that self-sacrifice in His path is sweet, not the pursuit of pleasure.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swears that self-sacrifice in His path is sweet, not the pursuit of pleasure; a concise statement of the joy of sacrifice.

selected.text: O Baha'u'llah! May my life be sacrificed for Thee! O Baha'u'llah! May my soul be offered up for Thy sake!
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Try to sacrifice something for the believers. Do not keep away from them, but give up everything you have.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urges the Kinneys and others to sacrifice something for the believers and not keep away from them; a direct practical counsel.

selected.text: A hundred thousand living hearts are needed on this path … To sacrifice a hundred lives with every breath
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s verses say a hundred thousand living hearts are needed on this path, to sacrifice a hundred lives with every breath; poetic intensity.

selected.text: the loved ones of God must sacrifice their lives for one another and prefer others' good to their own benefit
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that the loved ones of God must sacrifice their lives for one another and prefer others’ good to their own; a direct statement of preference for others.

selected.text: Faithfulness demands self-sacrifice and the giving up of one's life in the Path of that Beloved of the regions.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that faithfulness demands self-sacrifice and the giving up of life in the path of the Beloved; a concise principle.

selected.text: The wise soul sacrifices his life for a mighty Cause, not for dust--for the life of souls, not for their death.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that the wise soul sacrifices his life for a mighty Cause, for the life of souls and not their death; the contrast with warfare named in the why.

selected.text: when she sacrificed her life and soul for Christ, observe how she shone like a star from the horizon of the world
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says that a woman who sacrificed her life and soul for Christ shone like a star; a historical example from the Christian past.

selected.text: nay rather they may adore each other and sacrifice their wealth, comfort, life and spirit for the sake of each other.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes the friends may adore each other and sacrifice wealth, comfort, life and spirit for one another; a clear statement of mutual sacrifice.

selected.text: May my life, my inmost being, my soul and my body be offered up as a sacrifice for the dust ennobled by His footsteps.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: We have sacrificed Our very selves and Our spirits for the salvation of the world, and God is cognizant of what I say.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declares that He has sacrificed His very self and spirit for the salvation of the world; a direct statement of redemptive purpose.

selected.text: The spirit is beloved if it be sacrificed in Thy path, and the body acceptable if it be cast upon the dust in Thy name.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer says the spirit is beloved if sacrificed in God’s path and the body acceptable if cast on the dust; a concise devotional principle.

selected.text: O God! I am prepared to meet all calamities in Thy way and desire every trouble for Thy sake with all my heart and soul
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer declares readiness to meet all calamities and desire every trouble for God’s sake; prayer of readiness.

selected.text: Thou seest Thy loved ones, detached from their homes … They have borne hardships by land and sea, drawing nigh unto Thee
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words describe loved ones detached from their homes who bore hardships by land and sea; closes the lament section.

selected.text: The wandering led to distress, and the restlessness caused illness. He became sick and weak, separated and without remedy
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes one whose wandering led to distress and illness until he was sick, weak and without remedy; keeps the narrative setting of care for a suffering wanderer.

selected.text: My God, my God! This is my spirit, my soul, my body, and my limbs. I desire to sacrifice them in Thy love and in Thy path.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words offer spirit, soul, body and limbs to be sacrificed in God’s love; a short devotional self-offering.

selected.text: You offered up your life and material possessions. You considered it a blessing when your homes were looted and plundered.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells believers they offered life and possessions and counted the plunder of their homes a blessing; persecution recorded through its victims.

selected.text: How sweet, O my God, is the poison of death in Your love, and how delicious is the bitterness of annihilation in Your path
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer says how sweet is the poison of death in God’s love and the bitterness of annihilation in His path; personal petition.

selected.text: Therefore, if you seek eternal life, become a sacrifice, and if you desire endless existence, become effaced and evanescent.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that whoever seeks eternal life must become a sacrifice and whoever desires endless existence must become effaced; a concise paradox.

selected.text: The condition of faithfulness among the loved ones is to bear great hardship so they may arise with the mystery of sacrifice
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that faithfulness among the loved ones is bearing great hardship so they may arise with the mystery of sacrifice; joins endurance to the mystery.

selected.text: This station is the mystery of sacrifice, whether outwardly realized or not - the essential thing is to arise to this station
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that the mystery of sacrifice holds whether or not it is outwardly realized, and that the essential thing is to arise to this station; a key qualification for those not called to die.

selected.text: that is, the crop which those fathers planted, these sons are watering; the palm tree which they planted, these are nurturing
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes sons watering the crop and nurturing the palm their fathers planted; the image of inheritance as active responsibility.

selected.text: Though this wish of mine be the wish of a human creature, yet Thou knowest that my true wish is to sacrifice myself in Thy path.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: If you harbor thoughts of preserving your life, come not here … But if you would sacrifice soul and heart, come and bring them too
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s verses say that whoever harbours thoughts of preserving life should come not here, but whoever would sacrifice soul and heart should come; the invitation in verse.

selected.text: We have sacrificed Our souls in the path of God and summon all from the horizon of tribulation unto God, the Possessor of Names.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh states that He has sacrificed His soul in God’s path and summons all from the horizon of tribulation; His sacrifice joined to His summons.

selected.text: True faithfulness is when I become wandering and nameless and in the field of sacrifice become the target of the arrow of cruelty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says true faithfulness is becoming wandering and nameless and the target of cruelty in the field of sacrifice; his own definition of faithfulness.

selected.text: However much you may wail and cry out, and seek to sacrifice your life in the path of that Kind Beloved, it is fitting and worthy
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a grieving soul that however much they wail and seek to sacrifice life in the path of the Beloved, it is fitting; gives voice to sorrow within devotion.

selected.text: Though they may fear for their bodies, We do not fear, for We have sacrificed Our body in the love of God, the Exalted, the Great.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says that though others fear for their bodies He does not, having sacrificed His body in the love of God; fearlessness of the Manifestation.

selected.text: some, like Zulaykha, yearned for union with the Beloved, sacrificing life and wealth and honor and name and reason and understanding
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes some who, like Zulaykhá, sacrificed life, wealth, honour and reason for union with the Beloved; a literary image of longing.

selected.text: To sacrifice one's life in this station is the greatest gift in the human world and the cause of nearness to the Threshold of the Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls sacrifice of life in this station the greatest gift in the human world and a cause of nearness; a concise statement of its worth.

selected.text: All this, my God, hath come to pass in Thy path and happened for love of Thee, while Thy loved ones are aflame with the fire of Thy love
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer laments that all this happened in God’s path while His loved ones burn with His love; lament in prayer.

selected.text: Sacrifice this earthly frame for the Celestial Beloved and offer this contingent temple as an oblation to the Beloved of the realms beyond
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, in the Tablet to Badi‘ in Haifa, bids one offer this earthly frame as an oblation to the Beloved of the realms beyond; His own call to self-offering.

selected.text: And this bounty is yours because you preferred another over yourself, as it is stated in the Qur'an: "and prefer others before themselves."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a recipient that a bounty is his because he preferred another over himself, citing the Qur’anic “and prefer others before themselves”; links preference for others with scripture.

selected.text: In this day service at the sacred Threshold of the Blessed Beauty and steadfastness in the Cause of His love is the real sacrifice of the self.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that service at the Threshold and steadfastness in the Cause of love are the real sacrifice of self; closes the opening with sacrifice as lived service.

selected.text: After enduring great hardships, he took his heart and soul in hand, hastened to the altar of love, and offered them in the path of the Beloved.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá narrates one who, after great hardship, took heart and soul in hand and offered them at the altar of love; a concise martyrdom account.

selected.text: Man tasteth the cup of death but once; now if this should come to pass for the sake of God, its fragrance would perfume the world of existence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says man tastes death but once and that death for God’s sake would perfume the world; a memorable image of martyrdom’s influence.

selected.text: I love to sacrifice myself in Thy love and good-pleasure, and to be protected for the manifestation of Thy Cause and the exaltation of Thy Word.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer says He loves to sacrifice Himself and also to be protected for the manifestation of the Cause; holds sacrifice and preservation together.

selected.text: Indeed your absence causes hardship for your relations, but since it is in the path of the Lord it causes no harm, rather it is a bounty itself.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá acknowledges that a teacher’s absence causes hardship for relations but calls it a bounty because it is in the Lord’s path; a qualification touching family circumstances.

selected.text: Sacrifice of life is of two kinds. To be killed for the Cause is not so difficult as to live for it in absolute obedience to the commands of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishes two kinds of sacrifice of life and says living for the Cause in obedience is harder than being killed for it; a necessary qualification.

selected.text: He had been especially touched by the gifts of some children in America who had saved car fares by walking and given the money to the Temple fund.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá is recorded as touched by American children who walked to save car fares for the Temple fund; the guide’s example of a modest gift.

selected.text: Would ye slay Him Who hath sacrificed His soul in the path of God and made known unto you what the Most High, the Most Great, hath desired for you?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks whether they would slay Him Who sacrificed His soul to make known God’s desire for them; confronts opponents with His sacrifice.

selected.text: Thus may they attain that attitude of sacrificing even life for one another. For the love of one another they should sacrifice all that is possible.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes the friends sacrifice even life for one another and all that is possible for love of one another; returns to mutual love.

selected.text: Say: Sacrifice them, O people, in My path - this is the true sacrifice in the love of the All-Merciful, which none comprehend save the sincere ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calls this the true sacrifice in the love of the All-Merciful, comprehended only by the sincere; an early statement of the subject in His own words.

selected.text: How sweet is the deadly poison suffered in Thy path, and how precious are the arrows of Thy enemies when encountered for the exaltation of Thy Word!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer says how sweet is the deadly poison suffered in God’s path and how precious the arrows of enemies for His Word; complete devotional statement.

selected.text: Under chains and fetters, like a lion in the jungle of detachment, he was engaged with utmost joy and delight in offering praise and glorification
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes a prisoner who, under chains like a lion of detachment, offered praise with utmost joy; a narrative of joy in suffering.

selected.text: Every stone of that building, every stone of the road leading to it I have with infinite tears and at tremendous cost, raised and placed in position
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: God be praised!" he said. "Nothing is left me on this pathway. I have lost everything, including my bride. I have been able to give Him all I possessed
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, in Memorials of the Faithful, records one who said he had lost everything, even his bride, and given all he possessed; a narrative of total offering.

selected.text: The might of the divines and rulers did not prevent Him from speaking the word of truth. He spoke that which was the cause of exaltation and ascension
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says the might of divines and rulers did not prevent Him from speaking the word of truth; endurance of the Revealer under opposition.

selected.text: Turn ye unto your Creator and slay your souls in the path of God, the Truth, in humility before God, the Most High, for God is mighty and praiseworthy.
selected.reason: The Báb, in the Qayyumu’l-Asma’, calls people to turn to their Creator and slay their souls in God’s path in humility; the Báb’s call opens the Abraham section.

selected.text: My health, comfort, life and death are of no importance - may a hundred thousand like me be sacrificed for a single hair of the Temple of God's Cause.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says his health, comfort, life and death are of no importance beside a single hair of the Cause; personal devotion.

selected.text: The True One, glorified be His majesty, left His homeland and chose exile so that this exile might lead the exiles of the earth to their true homeland.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says the True One chose exile so that this exile might lead the exiles of the earth to their true homeland; a memorable image of revelation’s sacrifice.

selected.text: He must live for ever in the station of sacrifice and be ready to forgo all his material conditions. That is why it is so difficult, extremely difficult.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says one must live for ever in the station of sacrifice, ready to forgo all material conditions, and admits how difficult this is; an honest qualification.

selected.text: Would that every calamity might rain upon `Abdu'l-Baha in this way that he could become a ransom for the suffering of the friends of the Ancient Beauty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wishes every calamity might fall on himself that he might be a ransom for the suffering of the friends; expresses ransom as care for others.

selected.text: Consider how they gloried in sacrificing themselves for a piece of earth, and how much more one should pride himself in sacrificing for the Lord of Hosts!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá notes that people glory in sacrificing themselves for a piece of earth and asks how much more one should for the Lord of Hosts; a pointed comparison.

selected.text:
O sacrifice of God, from love's altar-place
Turn not back, but give thy life in love's ways … And this sacrifice returned not alive from the altar-place
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh quotes the verse “O sacrifice of God, from love’s altar-place, Turn not back” and notes this sacrifice returned not alive; poetry within the persecution accounts.

selected.text: endured in Baha's path every hardship and affliction … They left no abuse except that they inflicted it upon your precious body and tortured you severely
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addresses one who endured every hardship and severe torture in Bahá’s path; testimony to physical suffering.

selected.text: I beseech Thee not to disappoint me of that which Thou hast ordained for Thy chosen ones and trustees who have sacrificed their wealth and souls in Thy path.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer asks not to be disappointed of what was ordained for the chosen ones who sacrificed wealth and souls; closes the personal petitions.

selected.text: On the contrary man should be willing to accept hardships for himself in order that others may be happy... This is characteristic of man, this is becoming to man
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that man should accept hardship for himself so that others may be happy, calling this becoming to man; a plain principle of everyday sacrifice.

selected.text: in thy land and in the Land of Qaf; and uplift a special magnification over the Name of God, the Sacrificed (al-Dhabih); for, in very truth, He sacrificed His Self in the path of His Lord -- with a sacrifice such as is accounted in the path made straight
selected.reason: The Báb, in the Kitabu’l-Karim, magnifies the Name of God “the Sacrificed” (al-Dhabih), who sacrificed His Self in the path of His Lord; the ransom language in the Báb’s writing.

selected.text: This righteous deed brought great joy, that the handmaidens of the All-Merciful are so self-sacrificing and are among those who sacrifice their wealth and lives.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejoices that the handmaidens of the All-Merciful are so self-sacrificing that they give their wealth and lives; recognizes women’s concrete offerings.

selected.text: If any occasion befalleth and cases of tests come up, they will sacrifice their precious lives for the sake of the friends and freely give all their possessions.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes friends who in times of test would sacrifice their lives and freely give their possessions for one another; a further practical picture of solidarity.

selected.text: The attributes of generosity, of munificence and magnanimity can only be manifested in the reality of man when he ariseth to sacrifice himself in the path of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that generosity, munificence and magnanimity become manifest in a person only when he arises to sacrifice himself; links sacrifice with the qualities it releases.

selected.text: freely offer up heart and soul. Otherwise this journey will never reach its end, the goal will remain unattained, and the Beloved will not unveil His countenance.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that without freely offering heart and soul the journey will never end and the Beloved will not unveil His face; completes the lover’s condition.

selected.text: Therefore this is the time for steadfastness and the moment for glad-tidings, the day of sacrifice and the time of joy - and sacrifice is the essence of success.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls this the day of sacrifice and the time of joy, and says sacrifice is the essence of success; a concise statement.

selected.text: Would that thou possessed a myriad castles and lofty mansions, mighty palaces and edifices, so that every day one were destroyed in the path of the Best-Beloved.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wishes one possessed a myriad mansions so that one might be destroyed each day in the path of the Beloved; a memorable image of joyful giving.

selected.text: By God! Wert thou to find the sweetness of My remembrance, thou wouldst sacrifice thyself in My path and arise among the handmaidens with My remembrance and praise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says that if a handmaiden found the sweetness of His remembrance she would sacrifice herself in His path; addresses women directly.

selected.text: In the divine days he sacrificed in the path of the Friend all that he possessed. All the Concourse on High desired to make the sacrifice, but He did not accept it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says one sacrificed all he possessed in the path of the Friend, while the Concourse on High desired the sacrifice he was not permitted; an unusual narrative of acceptance.

selected.text: Pure souls have never been concerned with their own comfort and ease. Rather, solely for the enlightenment of all, they have forsaken sweetness and endured the sting.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that pure souls have never sought their own comfort but endured the sting for the enlightenment of all; names the purpose of self-giving.

selected.text: Dear Lord, if I were to sink into oblivion, if I were to be forgotten like Victoria, still I should want to pour out my life as a sacrifice to Thee for love of Thee.
selected.reason: The visitor’s words in this record of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to Juliet Thompson, wishing to pour out her life as a sacrifice even if forgotten; keeps the visitor’s words named in the group’s why.

selected.text: of disappointment, that we might bear every hardship, that in the very clay of our being might be kneaded the pure intent of service to the Cause of God, and that we might become, in self-sacrifice, wholly involuntary---finding no rest for a moment, seeking
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that in the very clay of our being the pure intent of service might be kneaded and that we become wholly self-sacrificing; a memorable image of personal devotion.

selected.text: It is my prayer that thou mayest become a moth that burns its wings in the flaming candle of the love of God, a salamander of love and desire in the fiery path of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that one become a moth burning its wings in the candle of God’s love and a salamander in the fiery path; the moth and candle image.

selected.text: Arise by God's leave and make mention of Him. He will protect thee, and He hath power over all things. Thus hath the Pen taught thee. Arise and fear not the oppressors.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids one arise by God’s leave, make mention of Him and fear not the oppressors; counsel against fear in sacrifice.

selected.text: Grant that I may sacrifice my life and attain to my heart's desire, that I may place the crown of bounty upon my head and raise the cry of 'O Glory of the Most Glorious!'
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays to sacrifice his life and attain his heart’s desire, raising the cry “O Glory of the Most Glorious!”; personal petition.

selected.text: In reality she is attracted and will bear every calamity and trial in the path of the Blessed Perfection and this very thing will be conducive to her spiritual development.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says a woman who bears every trial in the path of the Blessed Perfection will find it conducive to her spiritual development; relates hardship to growth.

selected.text: O Dhabih! When thou desirest the station of sacrifice in complete evanescence, accept no alteration. Sacrifice thyself for love of God, thy Lord and the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Dhabih accept no alteration when he desires the station of sacrifice in complete evanescence; returns to the Dhabih image.

selected.text: Take up such a work that the self-sacrificing ones of the past are forgotten, and hasten to the divine altar of sacrifice in such a way that offering one's life becomes bliss.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urges a work so great that past self-sacrificing ones are forgotten, until offering one’s life becomes bliss; an ambitious summons.

selected.text: Reflect upon Khadijah of a former time. Neither wealth nor property, neither blame nor persecution prevented her from God. She sacrificed her life and gave freely of her wealth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh holds up Khadijah, whom neither wealth, blame nor persecution kept from God, who gave her life and wealth; a historical example of offering.

selected.text: showing such self-sacrifice in the path of the Intended Lord that it becomes evident and manifest that these souls are indeed the worthy successors of those noble predecessors
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes souls will show such self-sacrifice that they are clearly worthy successors of their noble predecessors; inheritance as renewed sacrifice.

selected.text: A mother who sacrifices such a precious gem in the path of God is herself a pearl from the shell of faith and certitude and a brilliant jewel from the ocean of grace and bounty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls a mother who sacrificed such a precious gem a pearl from the shell of faith; honours a bereaved mother.

selected.text: If in this age of the bounty of the Blessed Beauty one does not sacrifice his life, in what other century of the world's centuries will he seek exaltation, ascent and progress?
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks in what other century one will seek exaltation if not by sacrifice in this age; urgency of this Day.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids hearers forget personal danger and have no fear in the cause of unity and peace; ends this section with overcoming fear.

selected.text: Consider that giving one's life in this battle is finding life - Christ waged battle upon the cross and at the moment of sacrificing His life was victorious over kings and subjects.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that giving one’s life in this battle is finding life, as Christ on the cross was victorious; links sacrifice to life gained.

selected.text: That which causes the brow to shine with manifest light is to arise with utmost strength in this mighty Cause and to sacrifice oneself in the path of the Lord of mercy and compassion
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that what makes the brow shine is arising with strength in the Cause and sacrificing oneself; links sacrifice with active service.

selected.text: Until you give your life, you will not reach the Beloved; until you become detached, you will not attain; until you burn, you will not illuminate; until you weep, you will not laugh
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that until you give your life you will not reach the Beloved, until you burn you will not illuminate; paradoxes of lover and beloved.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh testifies that the Manifestation forsook rest and chose abasement and exile for the elevation and glory of the world; the purposes of revelation’s sacrifice.

selected.text: According to the ordinances of the Bible, anyone committing a sin must offer a sacrifice. When Christ appeared He desired to make a symbol of Himself, so He said 'I am the atonement'.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that under the Bible’s ordinances sin required an offering and Christ made a symbol of Himself as the atonement; explains the atonement setting.

selected.text: Therefore, in thanksgiving for this most great bounty and supreme favor, one must take the divine cup in hand and, dancing in the arena of sacrifice, bestow it upon all created things.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids one take the divine cup and, dancing in the arena of sacrifice, bestow it on all created things; the cup shared with others.

selected.text: Where are those souls of whom He says "and give them preference over themselves, even though poverty be their own lot"? And where are those souls who act for God's sake and turn to God?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks where those souls are who give others preference over themselves even in poverty; a searching question on self-preference.

selected.text: The Glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of favors be upon the people of Baha who have not been frightened by the hosts of the world nor weakened by the power of the wicked ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blesses the people of Bahá who were neither frightened by the hosts of the world nor weakened by the wicked; courage under opposition.

selected.text: This is among the greatest of divine favors that He bestows the mighty profit of being sacrificed in His path upon souls that would certainly depart this world without benefit or fruit
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls being sacrificed in His path a mighty profit for souls who would otherwise depart without fruit; frames sacrifice as gain.

selected.text: You wrote about the difficulty of affairs for the teachers. The state of Christ's apostles is known - when teachers live in utmost difficulty, it has a profound effect on seeking souls.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá notes that when teachers live in utmost difficulty, as Christ’s apostles did, it profoundly affects seeking souls; explains the effect of sacrifice on others.

selected.text: Give up your head that you may raise it like a banner. Scatter your life that you may plant the sapling of hopes and desires in the garden of the bounty of His Holiness the Divine Unity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids one give up the head to raise it like a banner and scatter life to plant the sapling of hopes; the planting image named in the group’s why.

selected.text: Surely you know with what joy and delight the faithful friends drank that brimming cup, and how they hastened to the altar of love crying "O rapture! O joy! O glad tidings! O blessedness!"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls the faithful friends hastening to the altar of love crying “O rapture! O joy!”; the martyrs’ joy in their own words.

selected.text: Faithfulness and purity lie in freely sacrificing our lives and offering up our comfort, ease, joy and delight in His path. For love of Him is the soul's repose and the conscience's comfort.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says faithfulness lies in freely sacrificing life and comfort, for love of Him is the soul’s repose; joins faithfulness with comfort found in love.

selected.text: He is of those souls concerning whom the Primal Point hath said: "Verily I, and all who dwell in Paradise, do truly yearn, with utmost yearning, for the soul that hath been slain in His path
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh cites the Primal Point’s words of yearning for the soul slain in His path; closes the persecution accounts with the Báb’s voice.

selected.text: If thou seekest the eternal sovereignty of the world, sacrifice thy life like thy noble namesake. If thou desirest the crown of everlasting dominion, offer up thy head in the path of the Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids one who seeks eternal sovereignty to sacrifice life like his noble namesake and offer his head for the crown of everlasting dominion; a personal summons.

selected.text: The poisonous sting of the sword is preferable to them than all the panaceas that promise healing and the lethal arrows of cruelty seem to them to be a balm of faithfulness and sweet medicine.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes martyrs to whom the poisonous sword seems better than healing and the arrows of cruelty a balm; the inversion of suffering.

selected.text: Ye have borne in God's path that which none else hath borne … In truth, ye have heard taunts and witnessed abasement, and for the sake of God ye have renounced all that pertaineth to the world
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells believers that they have borne taunts and abasement and renounced the world for God’s sake; recognizes endurance under reproach.

selected.text: become the target of the taunts, curses, abuse, charges of unbelief and immorality, and doubts of the nations, so that you may receive a drop from the ocean of tribulations of the Ancient Beauty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá invites believers to bear taunts, curses and charges of unbelief to receive a drop of the tribulations of the Ancient Beauty; a distinctive form of sacrifice through reproach.

selected.text: They who have sacrificed their souls in My path are of the people of Baha. The Concourse on High will seek blessings from the dust of their footsteps. O blessed be this glorious, mighty station!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declares that those who sacrificed their souls in His path are of the people of Bahá, whose footsteps the Concourse on High blesses; praise of the station.

selected.text: I passed not by a tree but My heart addressed it saying: 'Would that thou wert cut down in My name and My body were crucified upon thee in God's path.'" By God! If the servants were to drink the wine hidden in this exalted word, it would suffice them and the intoxication of love
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounts that His heart addressed every tree, wishing it cut down and His body crucified upon it in God’s path; a memorable image echoed later by ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.

selected.text: O Amin! Reflect upon the lovers in all regions who, with perfect submission and contentment, have sacrificed their souls - the most exalted and precious of all things - for the One True Beloved.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Amín reflect on lovers everywhere who with submission and contentment sacrificed their souls; opens the accounts of persecution.

selected.text: "Die if you would be a devoted lover, for you have done all else yet still live," and cried out with his heart's tongue: "Kill me, kill me, O trustworthy ones, for in my death is life upon life."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the verses “Die if you would be a devoted lover” and “in my death is life upon life”; the paradox of poetry.

selected.text: How ignorant are the people! They are willing to forfeit their possession, honor, wealth, property and even life in the path of their country but unwilling to do any sacrifice in the path of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes that people will forfeit everything for their country but will not sacrifice in the path of God; a pointed comparison.

selected.text: She was astir and restless every hour of her life. Moth-like she circled in adoration round the undying flame of the Divine Candle, her spirit ablaze and her heart consumed by the fire of His love.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: the ocean of sincerity can be tasted, nor a breath of fragrant air inhaled from the rosegarden of the All Glorious without this level of sacrifice. O ye true friends! selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells the friends that no sweetness of sincerity is tasted without sacrifice and bids them be kind and sacrificing toward one another; opens the theme of mutual care.

selected.text: the scene of sacrifice is seen bedecked with such splendid pageantry, such marvellous festivity that the holy ecstasy of its wine seizeth forevermore the minds of those that are godly and spiritual
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes the scene of sacrifice bedecked with festivity whose holy ecstasy seizes the godly; opens the lament section with its paradox.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by the rustling of the Divine Lote-Tree and the lights of Thy Throne, O Lord of all beings, to make me one of those who have sacrificed their souls and all they possessed in Thy path.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer asks to be made one of those who sacrificed souls and possessions in God’s path; petition for the station.

selected.text: I am aware of all the afflictions, trials, hardships and tribulations that have befallen you, and I know how difficult these days have been and how obstinate these oppressive and ignorant people are.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells sufferers he is aware of their afflictions and how hard these days with oppressive people have been; keeps pastoral sympathy beside the summons.

selected.text: He left behind family and kin in the prime of youth and springtime of life … He was persecuted, O my God, by all peoples and enemies, and was burned by the fire of their hatred blazing to the heavens
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer recalls one who left family in the prime of youth and was burned by the fire of enemies’ hatred; remembrance of a young life.

selected.text: What! Art thou so attached to thy donkey that thou canst not leave it behind, while I have left everything, palace, villages, comfort and wealth? Hast thou not yet learned the lesson of severance
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a traveler whether he is so attached to his donkey that he cannot leave it, while He has left palace and wealth; a narrative lesson in severance.

selected.text: And the Spirit mourneth, saying: I would sacrifice myself that there might not befall Thee that which would sadden Thy heart … I have chosen, in My love for Thee, the afflictions of all who are on earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh records the Spirit’s mourning wish to sacrifice itself and His choice of the afflictions of all on earth; sacrifice voiced as love.

selected.text: Thanks be to God that He has trained such friends and raised up such souls beneath the shade of the Word of Unity, who freely sacrifice their wealth, lives, name and fame in the path of that Kind Beloved.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá gives thanks that God has raised souls who freely sacrifice wealth, lives, name and fame; recognizes a community of sacrifice.

selected.text: Make me the target for arrows aimed at Thy loved ones and the mark for spears directed at the hearts of Thy chosen ones, that I may sacrifice for them my spirit, essence, body, being, reality and identity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays to be the target of arrows aimed at God’s loved ones that he may sacrifice his being for them; sacrifice on behalf of others.

selected.text: I have not preserved myself for even an hour, and I have been as a burning fire among Thy sinful servants, as a shining lamp before Thine enemies, and as the rising sun above the heads of the wretched ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says He never preserved Himself for an hour and was as a burning fire and shining lamp among His enemies; a vivid self-description.

selected.text: My soul be a sacrifice for Thee, O Thou Who hast offered up Thyself for the salvation of the world. My spirit be a ransom for Thy prison, O Thou Who hast borne tribulations for the life of all in the lands
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words, “My soul be a sacrifice for Thee, O Thou Who hast offered up Thyself for the salvation of the world”, frame sacrifice for the life of all; devotional address to the sacrificed One.

selected.text: Blessed, then blessed is he who purposed to seek the Purpose of the world and sacrificed his spirit when the clamor of the nations was raised, in the path of God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blesses the one who sought the Purpose of the world and sacrificed his spirit when the nations clamoured; praise of steadfast sacrifice.

selected.text: As to what thou didst mention concerning Hasan whose hand was severed in the path of God, the Lord of all men, by My life! We shall surely give him wings wherewith to soar in the atmosphere of the Kingdom
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh promises that Hasan, whose hand was severed in God’s path, will be given wings to soar; a specific narrative of reward.

selected.text: Any soul that does not sacrifice in the path of the beloved that soul is lower than the body itself. Any head that is not offered as a sacrifice in the path of the beloved of the world is lower than the foot.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says a soul that does not sacrifice in the Beloved’s path is lower than the body and a head not offered is lower than the foot; a pointed inversion.

selected.text: That which thou didst mention caused boundless joy, for thou art prepared to sacrifice thy spirit and carry out the decree. Well is it with thee! This truly is the station of lovers on the Day of the Covenant.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh rejoices at one prepared to sacrifice his spirit, calling it the station of lovers on the Day of the Covenant; affirms readiness.

selected.text: For example if they bring me under the sword of the executioner and threaten me that unless I deny my belief they will behead me I will sacrifice my life in His Holiness' Path with the utmost joy and happiness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says that if threatened with beheading unless he denied his belief he would give his life with utmost joy; a personal testimony of steadfastness.

selected.text: In any case, we exiles are in utmost contentment and joy, even yearning and longing for sacrifice. O Lord! Ordain for Thy poor and helpless servant to drink from that cup which overflows with Thy great bounty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes that the exiles are content and joyful, yearning for sacrifice, and prays to drink from that cup; exile in his own voice.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh addresses one who left his homeland out of love for God and surrendered his spirit in His love; remembrance in His words.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes that service requires sacrificing everything and that he entrusted her to the Blessed Beauty and proceeded with the sea voyage; a family circumstance in service.

selected.text: His holiness the Christ loved both his disciples and believers to such an extent that he sacrificed his life for them. His holiness the Supreme (the Bab), loved the friends to such an extent that he gave his life for them
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says Christ loved His disciples so that He sacrificed His life for them, and the Báb likewise gave His life for the friends; ties the Manifestations’ sacrifice to love.

selected.text: In every breath, sacrifice thy life, and with every respiration become the target of an arrow, so that thou mayest sacrifice a hundred thousand lives for the Beloved and in every moment become a martyr in the path of the Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids one sacrifice life in every breath and in every moment become a martyr in the path of the Lord; the guide’s idea of continual living sacrifice.

selected.text: We are servants, offering up heart and soul in the path of the Beloved, and we count this as the greatest gift from the All-Merciful Lord … that he might be ready for sacrifice and through this sacrifice attain to true success
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes servants offering heart and soul as the greatest gift and readiness for sacrifice as the way to true success; links readiness and success.

selected.text: Baha'u'llah has assured us that this Cause will transcend every difficulty and will rise above every persecution but this condition will not be realized except through the self-sacrifice and infinite wisdom of believers of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that the Cause will rise above persecution only through the self-sacrifice and infinite wisdom of believers; pairs sacrifice with wisdom.

selected.text: One must sacrifice one's all in seeking the truth and become evanescent in its path so that one might obtain a portion from this ocean and be enlightened by a ray from its sun. This is what befits the truly wise and the discerning.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says one must sacrifice one’s all in seeking truth to receive a portion from its ocean; extends sacrifice to the search for truth.

selected.text: We testify that he hath taken for himself, beneath the canopies of My grandeur, a station whereunto none hath attained save him who hath sacrificed his spirit and all that he possessed in the path of God, the Lord of all religions.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh testifies that a departed soul attained a station reached only by those who sacrificed spirit and possessions; consolation through the station attained.

selected.text: "O sacrifice of God! Turn not back from love's altar, But give up thy life in the pathway of love" And whatever has befallen those holy souls in the path of God has surely not been without effect, and its fruit will certainly appear.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh quotes the same verse and adds that what befell those holy souls has not been without effect and its fruit will appear; joins martyrdom and fruit.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks God to turn His loved ones’ sorrow into joy and grant them the station of those who sacrificed wealth, souls and bodies; holds sorrow and hope together.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a wanderer in the path of God that this homelessness is sweeter than any home because it bears fruit; a memorable reversal.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says that since death is decreed, yielding life in the path of the All-Merciful is a thousand times better than dying in bed; a clear comparison on the value of a life’s end.

selected.text: O my God! If it is in accord with Thy divine wisdom, bestow upon me good health and encircle me with Thine own Confirmation and assistance; - in order that I may sacrifice my life on Thy Path, concentrate all my energies in Thy service
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays for health, if in accord with divine wisdom, so that he may sacrifice his life and concentrate his energies in God’s service; the health-for-service prayer named in the why.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says even a Bahá’í walks to the Kingdom only through obedient action and daily dying in self-sacrifice, how much more the Heralds of God; bridges personal and prophetic sacrifice.

selected.text: I took this holy spirit and this divine light and this lordly essence in the palm of my hands, desiring to sacrifice it at Thy feet. This is the ultimate purpose of my existence in Thy dominion and the final goal of my seeking in Thy lands.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describes taking His spirit and essence in His palm to sacrifice at God’s feet as the ultimate purpose of His existence; completes the Manifestation section.

selected.text: This is triumph and success, glory and prosperity, for servitude to God is proven and established under chains and fetters, and before arrow and sword, not at a sumptuous table with honey and sweetmeats and vintage wine and overflowing cups.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that servitude to God is proven under chains and before the sword, not at a sumptuous table; a decisive qualification.

selected.text: How many of the weak ones, after hearing the call, were seen to manifest such strength and power that neither the might and majesty of the world nor the massed ranks of the peoples could prevent them from turning to the Most Exalted Horizon.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá speaks of himself as a candle yearning for extinction, since extinction in God’s path is illumination; the guide’s candle image.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalls the man in Baghdad who severed his own head in rapture before Him; a striking historical narrative.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer remembers one who passed his days in bitterness and bore blame solely out of love; remembrance of hidden suffering.

The self-sacrifice and martyrdom of all the prophets caused the sins of the people to be forgiven. Self-sacrifice effaces discord, and causes man to attain virtues, changes darkness into light, hides the darkness of crime, and brings forth the light of good deeds. The mystery of it is explained in four ways. … Every one of the Manifestations of God is a perfect and accomplished being. They were all endowed with the divine characteristics, and have attained all the bounties and good deeds. For instance, the time between Moses and Christ was called the Day of Moses, and all the people who came in this time were called the branches of the Lote-tree of Moses, as they came in his time and under his command or revelation. … The Manifestations of God are likened unto the seeds. They contain all the perfections of the tree, but you can not see them until the tree grows up. The Blessed Lote-tree grew up from a single seed, yet all of the perfections and virtues which existed in the seed were not manifest until the seed sacrificed itself (its identity), that the tree might become apparent. The branches, leaves, flowers, fruit of the tree are only matter, but the perfection hidden in the seed has given to them color, fragrance and delicious taste. … When the tree attains its maturity and perfection you will also find the original seed appearing upon it, and the new seed signifies the second manifestation of the first, and of the second contains all of the perfections of the first. Thus the return of the first seed is apparent, but when the second seed grows into a tree the same leaves, branches, fruits do not appear, but the seed has sacrificed all of itself the same as the first, that the second tree may appear. The tree is matter, but the perfection hidden in the seed causes it to attain the vegetable kingdom. … Thus the disciples of Jesus Christ were but matter until they partook of the perfection of the seed of the Holy Spirit in the Body of Christ. Thus they attained spiritual growth. selected.text: A third disciple said, "To perform worthy deeds in the Kingdom we must be further self-sacrificing. From now on we should forego ease and bodily comfort, accept every difficulty, forget self and teach the Cause of God." This found acceptance and approval by all the others.

selected.text: Every action in the contingent world that emanates from physical susceptibilities is difficult; on the other hand, that which emanates from or owes its origin to the emotions of the conscience is easy. The least self-sacrifice that is based upon material origin seems to be arduous. For instance, it is difficult for man to sacrifice his ease or his possessions for racial love, but the giving of life in its entirety in the pathway of God is easy. Since self-sacrifice owes its origin to the emotions of the conscience man gladly offers his very life for a cause. Consider how willingly and with what great joy and happiness the disciples of Christ sacrificed their lives, because their love for their cause was based upon the emotions of the conscience. Had it been based upon the natural susceptibilities their sacrifice would have been very difficult if not impossible.
selected.reason: Explains willing self-sacrifice through spiritual love and conscience.

importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH06772 version a5777c032e414a823838e62f88a6e9ddab81fb14059a89ec23fc19eb3e52d816 paragraph4, metadata Y4, whose translations include PM#180x. The authorized paragraph reads “May my spirit be a sacrifice to the wrongs Thou didst suffer, and my soul be a ransom for the adversities Thou didst sustain”; the supplied wording reads “May my spirit be offered up for Thy hurt, and my soul be a sacrifice for Thy tribulations.” Omit; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB08891 version 4efdcc10e45980709ed7caad61dc24d8b99fc33e76be32ea51f1d7a94322e014 paragraph1, metadata Authorized empty, provisional (Star of the West, volume 14, issue 7). The provisional paragraph says that one who loses his “I-hood” becomes like iron which, cast in the fire, loses its coldness, blackness and solidity while heat, redness and glowing appear in it. The supplied wording, from (Abdu'l-Baha, in Response, p. 52), opens with a bracketed lead-in about the sword of self plunged into the fire of the love of God and says the iron’s coldness, darkness and hardness are concealed and it manifests heat, luminosity and fluidity. The image is the same but the wording is a different rendering, and the identification rests on a phrase review (score 0.357). Keep on merit as the guide’s only iron-and-fire passage and preserve approximate status.
